summary: AI-native companies are substituting tokens for labor at scale, with token spend reaching 20-50% of total comp at leading companies
summary_extended: Baker argues that AI-native companies are fundamentally restructuring their cost bases by substituting tokens for human labor at an unprecedented scale, with token spend as a percentage of total compensation reaching 20-25% at leading companies, 30% at Jasper (per Dylan Patel), and as high as 50% at some firms Baker has heard of anecdotally. The evidence is structural: gross profit dollars per FTE are rising sharply relative to prior startup generations, indicating that AI-native firms are scaling revenue without proportional headcount growth. Baker extrapolates this trend to a macro level, noting that with approximately $25 trillion in global knowledge work, even 20% token penetration implies $5 trillion in AI inference spend — sourced either from labor cost substitution or incremental economic growth enabled by AI productivity gains. The investment implication is that demand for inference compute and token-generating infrastructure is far larger and more durable than consensus expects, though Baker acknowledges the specific data points are not formally audited. No single publicly traded company is the direct subject of this thesis; rather, it is a structural demand argument for the AI inference ecosystem broadly.
